moments.selftext: We’re sharing a solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem, one of the deepest problems at the frontier of mathematics. The proof was produced by a group of agents, using an OpenAI next-generation model significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra. The problem concerns whether the description of smooth three-dimensional fluid motion modeled by the Navier-Stokes equations can break down. It has remained unresolved for roughly 90 years.

moments.selftext: I spent much of the weekend talking with the team who did this work. Seb--and everyone else--acted with integrity and generosity throughout. Initially we believed the other team had also solved the problem. We wanted to collaborate and do a joint release. When we learned that they had Euler but not Navier-Stokes, we offered to let them go first, to suggest that they should be the ones to get the prize, and optionally for Tristan to be the lead author on a rewrite of the OpenAI proof. We felt it was challenging to offer the same to Levent (an Anthropic employee), who was not willing to talk or coordinate with us anyway. We were open to other solutions. We would have greatly preferred coordination. We did not rush to publish even though the other team wasn't communicating with us. The team threatened us with unfounded accusations of plagarism. Now that we can see their work, the approaches appear to be different. It is also worth noting that our latest model can solve many, many other math problems. It is true that we tried this because there were rumors on the internet last week that Anthropic's models had solved a millennium problem and we were curious if ours could do it too.

moments.selftext: THIS IS HISTORY I don't know if you realize what this means. My hands are shaking... Are we seeing the first sign of emerging ASI (artificial superintelligence)? The implications of this make me think we’re past the point of just asking whether we’re on the verge of AGI (we possibly already are), and that we could be about to collide head-on with an exponential explosion of intelligence. The singularity... Straight to ASI! According to OpenAI, around 10,000 coordinated AI agents arrived at the solution in about 88 hours, plus another 17 for formalization and verification in Lean. moments.title: I love that the only monumental bronze equestrian statue from ancient Rome to survive is one of Marcus Aurelius—a man who had little concern for being remembered forever. The statue of Marcus Aurelius was likely created
moments.selftext: I love that the only monumental bronze equestrian statue from ancient Rome to survive is one of Marcus Aurelius—a man who had little concern for being remembered forever. The statue of Marcus Aurelius was likely created around 176 CE, following his military campaigns against Germanic tribes. Ancient Rome was once home to numerous monumental equestrian statues. Late Roman accounts mention 22 of these massive “great horses,” yet the statue of Marcus Aurelius is the only one that has survived intact. Its preservation was largely due to a historical misunderstanding. During the Middle Ages, people mistakenly believed the statue portrayed Constantine, the first Roman emperor to embrace Christianity. Because of this mistaken identity, it was spared while countless other ancient bronze statues were melted down and their valuable metal repurposed. That makes the statue’s survival particularly ironic. In Meditations, Marcus Aurelius often wrote about how fleeting fame, reputation, and human memory truly are. He believed that, with enough time, both those who are remembered and those who remember them will eventually disappear.

moments.selftext: New GTA 6 map details (previews): - Once you unlock free roam after some missions, you can go anywhere on the map without barriers or restrictions - The map is an island (Leonida) and doesn’t have a panhandle - It’s 2x the size of GTA5 and 3x the playable area of RDR2 - Vice City is double the size of Los Santos - The built-up area outside Vice City is 11 times bigger than the built-up area outside Los Santos - The map is dense, with 5 counties and approximately 10 cities/towns - There are multiple islands, and underwater exploration will feature diving equipment, shipwrecks and treasures - The map in the pause menu is very detailed with satellite 3D imagery - It helps you to plan a heist, as it shows buildings, gang bases, stores…etc in 3D, the loot value and the entry and exit - When the map is zoomed out, you only see the main roads and highways, but the more you zoom in, more roads and alleys appear - Rockstar’s goal is to make as many enterable buildings (there are hundreds of interiors) - Areas on the map won’t be fully visible until you explore them (fog of war) - There are many ways to fast travel around the map using public transport such as buses, trains, taxis, RydeMe app (Uber), Metromover and you can either skip the trip or talk with passenger NPCs and have full conversations or listen to the radio - You can buy as many garages around the map but you can’t buy safe houses (Jason & Lucia’s house changes throughout the story because they’re on the run) - Mission waypoints on the map are pink, custom ones are cyan -Mount Kalaga located in the northern part is the highest point in the map - You’ll be able to see heat areas on the map (an area where you committed a crime before and police will be on the lookout for you there for some time, as they actually setup a perimeter around the crime scene) - There heat area is red and there’s an even larger area around it in lighter red -At 6 stars, the heat area becomes map-wide - Any building with a helipad on top will be enterable and you can explore its interior, go up either by stairs or using the elevator to reach the top floor without loading screens
